 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Ja Morant's injury is an unfortunate development for the Portland Trail Blazers , but it could create a significant opportunity for Scoot Henderson. With Morant sidelined by a Grade 2 hamstring strain, Henderson has stepped into the starting lineup. However, this opportunity could mean much more than simply filling a spot while one of Portland's stars recovers.
 For Henderson, this might be his final chance to prove he can be the franchise point guard the Blazers envisioned when they selected him with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2023 NBA Draft.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement There has been plenty of uncertainty surrounding Henderson's long-term future in Portland. Injuries have interrupted his development, and his performance has yet to consistently match the expectations that come with being a top-three selection. The arrival of Morant only added another layer of uncertainty to his place in the team's future.
 Now, with Morant unavailable, Henderson has an opportunity to change that conversation.
 The Athletic's Jason Quick highlighted the significance of Portland naming Henderson as Morant's replacement in the starting lineup Saturday against the Utah Jazz, "One can understand, then, why it seemed so significant when Nori named Henderson as Morant's replacement in the starting lineup Saturday against the Utah Jazz. This, it seems, is Henderson's big chance. And perhaps his final chance. How Henderson guides the Blazers while Morant heals could either answer that burning question, or extinguish the idea for good."
 That is a pretty significant opportunity, especially considering the circumstances surrounding Portland's crowded backcourt. Morant is expected to be a major part of the franchise's plans moving forward, while Damian Lillard also remains in the picture. Henderson needs to show that he can be more than just another guard competing for minutes.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement This isn't necessarily about putting up huge scoring numbers every night. Portland needs to see Henderson take control of the offense, make his teammates better, limit turnovers and demonstrate that he can consistently make winning decisions. His ability to run the team and establish himself as a reliable floor general will be just as important as his individual production.
 There is still time for Henderson to develop, and it would be premature to write off a 22-year-old guard. However, the NBA is a results-driven business, and Portland needs to figure out what it has in Henderson before making long-term decisions about its backcourt.
 Morant's absence gives him the opportunity to make that decision a lot easier. Henderson has the starting job, the minutes and the ball in his hands. What he does with them could determine whether he remains part of Portland's long-term plans or becomes another former lottery pick who never quite lived up to his potential. This is likely his last chance in Portland.
